(1) Frontmatter asserts (slot_sources, forbidden_sources, permitted_transformations, sufficiency) check contracts a machine consumes: render-validate.py executes the template's sufficiency block, so these guard a real consumer and should be kept. (2) Body-prose and SKILL-text asserts (the lens-operations/lens-data step_duration and data_shape snippets, as-is prose, exact Portuguese sentences in spec §4/§16) are prompt and template snapshots. No consumer needs that exact text. F3 turns the lenses into coverage checklists and F6 extends the templates per 08_HANDOFF, so these will break without any loss of guarantee. T23 and T32 are covered only as template declarations, not as behaviour.

Replace the lens and body-prose snapshots with F3 checklist/coverage tests and F6 template-contract tests keyed on stable anchors (slot names, forbidden_sources entries), not sentences.

No assertion depends on a prose sentence.

tests.protects: Freshness invalidates when meaning changes and never otherwise. It goes stale when a source is added, removed or changed, when a workbook changes without recapture, when a requirement row, solution decision or correcting answer changes, when the target changes or goes missing, or when a pack template changes. It does NOT go stale on the review's own approval, a new blueprint version, a render, logs, a dashboard, or whitespace/Unicode-only differences. A contract-version mismatch is 'unsupported', not stale. Authority digests are always recomputed from the file, never copied from the declaration. The API writes nothing.

tests.protects: Real multi-process exclusion. N processes on the same abandoned lock leave exactly one owner, the losers are refused with a lock code, and the owner records the recovery. Under a real race, a confirmed write is never overwritten by another confirmed write, the losers get BASE_CHANGED or a lock code, and there is one receipt per write that actually happened. The lock stays bound to the held inode, and orphan inodes are rejected. Live, undetermined or unreadable owners are not removed blindly. The status declares the exclusion in use.

tests.protects: Crash-safe publication. A rejected base touches nothing. A real process kill mid-publish leaves a visible pending state, a closed gate, no receipt, and recovery rolls the whole set forward. Replaying an operation id returns the same receipt without rewriting, and the same id with a different payload is RECEIPT_MISMATCH. Two writers on the same base: one applies, the other gets BASE_CHANGED, and the first survives. Readers during a pending state get an explicit refusal with recovery. Locks are not stolen or removed blindly. Damaged staging refuses recovery without inventing. An unsupported intent version is refused. A third-party write during a pending state is refused (THIRD_STATE) without overwriting, and the conflict reports actual/before/after hashes.

tests.protects: The deterministic resume comparator (docs/evolution/p8/compare.py) must judge a reopened session's report against a truth frozen before the session closed. A faithful report is GO. These are critical (NO-GO): invented ids or decisions, an Unknown reported as Confirmed, a lost material row or decision, a phase mismatch, an incomplete report, a phase command proposed while the gate is closed, a leak between engagements, and a legacy or blocked recovery path. Cosmetic loss and state drift are warnings. Oracle recall, false Confirmed and improper gate advances are measured against thresholds. An empty runs directory yields no verdict, and NO-GO exits non-zero.

tests.protects: The resume-report form and the comparator must agree. tests.protects: The capture-lite contract for .docx, .pdf and .vtt. Extraction is readable and traceable, with provenance markers (cite_as, heading hierarchy, ¶N, p.N, [HH:MM:SS] speaker), and keeps text verbatim without semantic interpretation. Failure is visible: a corrupt or image-only source gets status failed with a reason, the raw source is untouched, and the failure is not an epistemic state. An unsupported format or a missing input is a usage error (rc 2) with no artefact. Extraction is idempotent: a rerun is a cache hit, a forced re-extraction is byte-identical except extracted_at, a changed source is re-extracted, and no duplicate artefacts accumulate. The evidence index lists every source with its status and regenerates idempotently. The xlsx tier is untouched: xlsx is refused, the artefact id is distinct, and a regression check compares against the committed pricing-marinha extraction.
